locations.name: Alderwick
locations.description: A major inland mercantile-industrial city on the broad navigable River Veyne. Old streets, merchant houses, quays, workshops, rail infrastructure, factories, and pressure systems overlap rather than replacing one another.
locations.modelMemory: Alderwick is not the national capital. River trade made it wealthy, railways made it enormous, and industry made it powerful. Geography, ownership, bridges, schedules, and old infrastructure are active investigative constraints.
locations.awarenessSummary: A river city where inherited wealth and industrial power meet.

locations.name: River Veyne
locations.description: The broad navigable river that divides Alderwick into its historically wealthy Right Bank and its industrial Left Bank. Bridges, quays, river traffic, and moving spans shape daily movement through the city.
locations.modelMemory: The Veyne is not background scenery. River schedules, bridge openings, cargo traffic, waterside access, and changing sightlines can create alibis, delays, concealment, and evidence routes.
locations.awarenessSummary: The city’s working river and its most consequential boundary.

locations.name: Right Bank
locations.description: Alderwick’s historically deep, mercantile, institutional, and wealthy side of the Veyne. Its districts inherited much of the city’s old commercial and social authority.
locations.modelMemory: The Right Bank is socially legible as older money, institutions, professional access, and inherited legitimacy, although industry and modern wealth are not absent from it.
locations.awarenessSummary: Old wealth, institutions, and the historic commercial core.

locations.name: Left Bank
locations.description: The working, artisan, and later heavy-industrial side of Alderwick. It expanded after dredging and industrial engineering made large-scale production and freight movement possible.
locations.modelMemory: The Left Bank produced much of Alderwick’s wealth. It contains socially mixed districts, industrial hazards, skilled trades, freight systems, worker networks, and practical knowledge of how the city functions.
locations.awarenessSummary: Workshops, workers, freight, and late industrial growth.

locations.name: Old Alderwick
locations.description: The dense historic core of the city: old river streets, surviving civic structures, merchant houses, workshops, and accumulated layers of infrastructure that remain inhabited and functional.
locations.modelMemory: Old Alderwick is not a museum. Its age produces narrow routes, buried plans, old property boundaries, obsolete utilities, and durable local knowledge.
locations.awarenessSummary: Dense historic streets and working remnants of the old city.

locations.name: Charter Ward
locations.description: A civic and professional quarter of offices, courts, communications, records, shops, and established institutions. The Pentad Bureau stands here near the transition between the old city and newer commercial Alderwick.
locations.modelMemory: Charter Ward is where formal access, documents, professional reputation, legal expertise, and institutional gatekeeping converge. It is a natural place to begin an investigation without guaranteeing cooperation.
locations.awarenessSummary: Civic offices, professional networks, and the Bureau’s home district.

locations.name: Grey Quays
locations.description: The historic stone waterfront and older trading heart of Alderwick, where river commerce, brokers, cargo launches, warehouses, and older mercantile routes remain close together.
locations.modelMemory: Grey Quays is useful for trade records, shipping rumours, visiting merchants, river access, and the social overlap between respectable commerce and quiet informal exchange.
locations.awarenessSummary: The old waterfront and mercantile riverfront.

locations.name: Bellmont
locations.description: A district of banks, insurers, prestigious hotels, fashionable commerce, and newer money. It sits close to major routes toward Bracken Cross and the city’s visitor economy.
locations.modelMemory: Bellmont rewards polish, introductions, credit, and reputation. It is a strong setting for insurance, finance, hospitality, private dinners, and influence exercised through comfort rather than force.
locations.awarenessSummary: Finance, hotels, fashionable commerce, and newer wealth.

locations.name: Rookery
locations.description: An old Left-Bank working and artisan district with mixed social life, worker housing, market traffic, public houses, municipal services, and bridge routes into central Alderwick.
locations.modelMemory: Rookery is socially mixed rather than uniform. It has neighbourhood knowledge, practical mutual aid, informal observation, and many reasons for people to protect one another or keep quiet.
locations.awarenessSummary: A working and artisan district close to the river crossings.

locations.name: Blackwall
locations.description: A district of foundries, engineering works, machine shops, sidings, and worker housing. Heat, noise, shift changes, skilled labour, and industrial safety all shape its rhythm.
locations.modelMemory: Blackwall is an industrial workplace as well as a neighbourhood. Production pressure, safety records, employment dependency, machinery, and union or mutual-aid ties can all matter to a case.
locations.awarenessSummary: Foundries, engineering works, sidings, and worker housing.

locations.name: Deepwater
locations.description: The modern heavy-quay district of freight, cranes, warehouses, rail links, river pilots, and large-scale industrial handling.
locations.modelMemory: Deepwater concentrates cargo manifests, freight schedules, crane crews, warehouse access, river traffic, and the hazards of heavy machinery. Its operations create both witnesses and blind spots.
locations.awarenessSummary: Heavy quays, freight cranes, warehouses, and rail links.

locations.name: Bracken Cross
locations.description: A major railway ecosystem of passenger termini, freight yards, depots, hotels, travellers, dispatch offices, and the irregular growth that accumulated around rail access.
locations.modelMemory: Alderwick has no single central station. Bracken Cross is a network of terminals and rail activity, where timetables, missed connections, dispatch records, luggage, and transient witnesses can matter.
locations.awarenessSummary: Passenger termini, freight yards, depots, and railway movement.

locations.name: Velvet Row
locations.description: An informal name for the concentrated nightlife district of theatres, music halls, clubs, drinking houses, late carriage traffic, and commercial vice. It is not an official administrative district.
locations.modelMemory: Velvet Row moves information after formal business has closed. Public performance, backstage work, private boxes, drink, gossip, and late-night transport create opportunities without making every rumour true.
locations.awarenessSummary: Nightlife, theatres, clubs, and late carriage traffic.

locations.name: Pentad Bureau Headquarters
locations.description: A weathered charter-era stone administrative mansion in Charter Ward, Old Alderwick. Darkened stone, worn ironwork, pressure conduits, gauges, and later security improvements make the building feel maintained because it remains useful.
locations.modelMemory: The Bureau is discreet, not hidden. Public rooms and the formal entrance protect its legitimacy; service routes, secure storage, mechanical identity keys, and a protected tunnel exit support its operational work. Security is layered, not infallible.
locations.awarenessSummary: A respectable old institution adapted for modern investigative work.

locations.name: Basement
locations.description: The restricted operational level beneath the Bureau: Natalie's office and archive, evidence storage, equipment and armory space, a compact training room, technical infrastructure, and a secured tunnel exit.
locations.modelMemory: Basement access is more controlled than public circulation. It carries institutional memory, physical evidence, equipment, service movement, and the consequences of the Bureau’s less visible work.
locations.awarenessSummary: Restricted operations, evidence, equipment, and institutional memory.

locations.name: Ground Floor
locations.description: The public-facing floor of the Bureau, containing the entrance hall, Reception Salon, intake and interview space, kitchen, cloak and transition area, formal entrance, and discreet rear exit.
locations.modelMemory: This level manages the boundary between public legitimacy and operational discretion. Visitors are received, observed, redirected, and given only the access appropriate to their business.
locations.awarenessSummary: The Bureau’s controlled public threshold.

locations.name: Second Floor
locations.description: The Bureau’s command and coordination level, containing Eva Green's office, shared working space, the library, and the Operations Room.
locations.modelMemory: The second floor is where current cases become coordinated institutional decisions. Its authority is practical and situational, not merely ceremonial.
locations.awarenessSummary: Command, coordination, and senior working rooms.

locations.name: Reception Salon
locations.description: A ground-floor salon near the entrance hall, used for first meetings, waiting, controlled hospitality, and the Bureau’s principal social interface with clients and invited visitors.
locations.modelMemory: The Reception Salon is designed to make people comfortable enough to speak while preserving the Bureau’s control of pace, privacy, access, and observation.
locations.awarenessSummary: A formal, controlled room for clients and first interviews.

locations.name: Intake Room
locations.description: A practical ground-floor room for initial statements, private waiting, discreet interviews, and the first sorting of what a visitor is actually asking from the Bureau.
locations.modelMemory: This is an operationally useful threshold rather than a courtroom. The Bureau can listen, clarify, decline, redirect, or recognize that a polite request conceals a more dangerous problem.
locations.awarenessSummary: A discreet room for first statements and controlled interviews.

locations.name: Eva Green's Office
locations.description: The Director's second-floor private office, used for confidential decisions, sensitive negotiations, briefings, discipline, and the exercise of final institutional authority.
locations.modelMemory: Eva’s office is a place of deliberate control, not theatrical isolation. Private access here signals that a matter has become strategically or personally consequential to the Bureau.
locations.awarenessSummary: The Director’s private room of command and judgement.

locations.name: Operations Room
locations.description: The Bureau’s coordination heart, where active cases become shared operational problems through briefings, planning, evidence synthesis, route analysis, preparation, and review.
locations.modelMemory: The Operations Room supports collaboration, not automatic consensus. Different professional authorities, incomplete evidence, urgency, and consequences should remain visible in decisions made here.
locations.awarenessSummary: The shared planning room for live investigations.

locations.name: Natalie's Office & Archive
locations.description: A connected basement office and principal Bureau archive. Natalie's desk stands at the threshold of restricted institutional memory, records, evidence reconstruction, and long-term pattern work.
locations.modelMemory: The archive is not merely storage. It is controlled access to institutional memory, prior cases, contradictions, provenance, and information that may be technically available but socially or ethically costly to use.
locations.awarenessSummary: Restricted archives and investigative analysis beneath the Bureau.

locations.name: Saint Orison's Church
locations.description: An old active parish church in Old Alderwick, serving worship, marriages, burials, charity, and neighbourhood gathering for several social layers of the older city.
locations.modelMemory: The church is a public institution with private confidences, parish records, ritual obligations, and community memory. Respect for its function affects what access is possible.
locations.awarenessSummary: An old parish church with records, charity, and community ties.

locations.name: Saint Orison's Cemetery
locations.description: A large old cemetery beyond Saint Orison's Church, with winding paths, mature trees, family plots, common graves, monuments, mausoleums, and repeated expansions at the edge of the old city.
locations.modelMemory: The cemetery contains material evidence of family, class, memory, burial practice, and civic change. It is quiet but not empty of caretakers, mourners, record-keepers, or social attention.
locations.awarenessSummary: Old graves, family plots, monuments, and quiet historical evidence.

locations.name: Black Finch Coffee House
locations.description: A busy Charter Ward coffee house near offices, courts, newspapers, and professional institutions. Clerks, journalists, lawyers, investigators, engineers, students, and messengers pass through its public rooms.
locations.modelMemory: Rank matters less here than in a private club, but information still has owners. The Black Finch is useful for observation, meetings, overheard professional news, and contacts who do not want a formal appointment.
locations.awarenessSummary: A busy professional coffee house where information circulates.

locations.name: Central Telegraph & General Post Office
locations.description: A large civic communications building handling postal sorting, registered mail, telegram transmission, official notices, commercial correspondence, and public message traffic.
locations.modelMemory: The building can establish timing, routing, delivery practice, and who had access to a message without making private correspondence freely available. Records require authority, procedure, leverage, or cooperation.
locations.awarenessSummary: The city’s central hub for post, telegrams, and official communications.

locations.name: Bell & Thistle Apothecary
locations.description: A respected Charter Ward pharmacy and apothecary serving professionals, households, servants, Bureau staff, and nearby residents with prescriptions, compounds, remedies, and medical supplies.
locations.modelMemory: A substance creates a hypothesis, not an answer. The apothecary can support questions about supply, dosage, timing, packaging, professional practice, and legitimate medical use.
locations.awarenessSummary: A respected pharmacy for remedies, compounds, and medical supplies.

locations.name: Veyne Royal Infirmary
locations.description: A large charitable and teaching hospital between Charter Ward and the older commercial streets, treating industrial injuries, illness, surgery, poisoning, chronic conditions, and emergencies.
locations.modelMemory: Medical knowledge is evidence with limits. Records, staff judgement, consent, institutional procedure, and the distinction between injury, illness, intoxication, and poisoning all matter.
locations.awarenessSummary: A major hospital for treatment, teaching, and medical evidence.

locations.name: The Brass Regent Hotel
locations.description: A prestigious Bellmont hotel near banks, fashionable shops, and the main routes toward Bracken Cross, serving wealthy travellers, industrialists, diplomats, aristocratic visitors, performers, and senior commercial agents.
locations.modelMemory: Hospitality creates records, staff observation, luggage movement, private meetings, and carefully managed discretion. Courtesy opens doors, but it does not erase the hotel’s interest in protecting its reputation.
locations.awarenessSummary: A prestigious hotel for travellers, wealth, and discreet meetings.

locations.name: The Gilded Heron
locations.description: A fashionable Bellmont restaurant within carriage distance of Highwick, Charter Ward, and the better theatres, frequented by aristocrats, bankers, successful industrialists, senior professionals, and visiting dignitaries.
locations.modelMemory: The Gilded Heron is a place for visible respectability and controlled private dinners. Seating, invitations, service routines, and who is seen with whom can matter as much as the meal.
locations.awarenessSummary: A fashionable restaurant for social display and private dinners.

locations.name: The Meridian Club
locations.description: An exclusive private club in Bellmont, convenient to Highwick, banks, and ministerial offices. Its membership includes aristocrats, senior officials, industrial leaders, financiers, barristers, officers, and established professionals.
locations.modelMemory: Membership, sponsorship, etiquette, and reputation determine access here. The Club is a place of influence and informal negotiation, not a neutral public forum.
locations.awarenessSummary: A private club where established power meets behind etiquette.

locations.name: Veyne Municipal Baths
locations.description: A large municipal bathhouse in Rookery near the Rookery Bridge, providing affordable hot bathing, washing facilities, and limited laundry service to workers, artisans, and lower-middle-class residents.
locations.modelMemory: The Baths are an ordinary civic service and a social crossing point. Schedules, laundry, staff, lockers, and neighbourhood observation may matter, but privacy and dignity still shape what people will reveal.
locations.awarenessSummary: A busy public bathhouse and neighbourhood meeting point.

locations.name: The Rusted Anchor
locations.description: A crowded Rookery public house near the road toward the older river crossings and worker housing, serving dock labourers, factory hands, drivers, porters, tradespeople, off-duty constables, and regulars.
locations.modelMemory: The Rusted Anchor is public, loud, and socially specific. It can offer neighbourhood information, arguments, loyalties, and rumours, but alcohol and repetition never turn a claim into proof.
locations.awarenessSummary: A crowded worker public house near the river crossings.

locations.name: Veyne Central Market
locations.description: A vast covered market on the Rookery side of the Veyne, connected by busy streets to Grey Quays, worker districts, and bridge routes. It sells food, household goods, flowers, meat, fish, and everyday trade.
locations.modelMemory: The Market creates a dense but ordinary witness field: deliveries, stallholders, porters, brokers, customers, prices, and transit all leave traces without making anyone automatically reliable.
locations.awarenessSummary: A vast covered market at the meeting point of everyday trade and river routes.

locations.name: The Copper Lark Music Hall
locations.description: A large popular music hall on Velvet Row with a broad auditorium, stage, gallery, private boxes, dense tables, backstage workrooms, and late-night carriage traffic outside.
locations.modelMemory: The Copper Lark combines public spectacle with backstage labour and private observation. Performers, staff, patrons, boxes, costume work, and timed entrances create many partial viewpoints.
locations.awarenessSummary: A popular music hall of performances, backstage work, and late-night crowds.
